question.text: If an investment earns a nominal return of 12% and inflation is 6%, the approximate real rate of return is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The exact real rate of return is computed using the Fisher relation: Real return = [(1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation)] - 1 = (1.12 / 1.06) - 1 = 1.0566 - 1 = 5.66%. The approximate shortcut of subtracting inflation from nominal (12% - 6% = 6%) is close but not precise, especially when inflation is meaningful. The Trap: 6.00% is the simple subtraction approximation, not the exact real rate. 18.00% mistakenly adds the two rates and 7.20% multiplies them — neither reflects how real return is computed. Note: The NISM Series X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook discusses nominal vs real return qualitatively and notes that inflation erodes purchasing power, but the explicit Fisher formula [(1+nominal)/(1+inflation)]-1 was not located in the workbook pages reviewed. The derivation above is presented as general personal-finance industry knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
